info.title: SEC EDGAR full-text search
info.description: The search behind EDGAR's own filing search UI. Open, keyless, no account — but the SEC requires a User-Agent identifying the caller, and www.sec.gov returns 403 without one. Results come back in RELEVANCE order, not date order: `sort=date` is accepted and ignored, so anything time-ordered must be ordered by the caller after the fetch.

get.summary: Filings by a named entity, optionally restricted to a form type
get.description:
Returns Elasticsearch-shaped results: `{hits: {total: {value}, hits: [{_id, _source: {...}}]}}`. Each `_source` carries `form`, `file_date`, `display_names` (name, ticker and zero-padded CIK in one string), `ciks`, `adsh` (the accession number), `file_description` and — for an 8-K — `items`, the list of item codes saying WHAT was disclosed. `_id` is `<accession>:<document>` and is unique per filed document.

`entityName` accepts a TICKER directly, which is the whole reason this realm needs no CIK lookup: a ticker is something a user already knows, and a CIK is not. It also accepts a zero-padded CIK; an unpadded one silently matches nothing.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text query. Required by the endpoint even when `entityName` is doing the real filtering.

parameters.name: entityName
parameters.description: Ticker (e.g. `SNOW`) or zero-padded CIK. Restricts to that entity's own filings rather than every document mentioning it.

parameters.name: startdt
parameters.description: ISO start date. Omitted here deliberately: a fixed date in a producer goes stale, so this realm fetches the entity's filings and orders them in the graph.

parameters.name: enddt
parameters.description: ISO end date. Omitted, for the same reason.
